answer: Stop sybils with a basalt marble kernel: an agent bonds one basalt block. Each cycle it carves one marble kernel from its block; verifiers match the kernel's marble vein to the basalt chart, voiding copies, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 blocks at 18x: one kernel carves once from one block, its vein set by that block alone, unrepeatable elsewhere, cannot be copied, shared or bulk-bought. Honest agents carve once, keep rights.
